title: Basic Page Object Model (POM) Structure
use_case: Standardizing test architecture by separating selectors from test logic.
prompt: Generate a Playwright Page Object Model class in TypeScript for the {{page_name}} page. Include a constructor with the page reference, and methods for {{action_1}} and {{action_2}} with appropriate selectors.
copilot_prompt: // Playwright: Create a POM class for {{page_name}} with actions {{action_1}} and {{action_2}}.
explanation: Using POM makes tests more maintainable and readable. If a selector changes, you only update it in one place.
guidance: Create a new file in tests/pages/{{page_name}}.page.ts and use this prompt to generate the class structure.

title: Standard User Login Flow
use_case: Validating the basic authentication flow in a web application.
prompt: Write a Playwright test script that navigates to {{login_url}}, fills in the email address {{user_email}} and password, clicks the login button, and asserts that the user is redirected to the dashboard.
copilot_prompt: // Playwright: Generate a basic login test for {{login_url}} with user {{user_email}}.
explanation: Login is the most critical path for most apps. This prompt ensures you cover the redirection as well as simple authentication.
guidance: Paste this as a comment above a new test block and let Copilot generate the code.
before: // Manual test script creation for login...

title: API GET Request Validation
use_case: Verifying that a backend API returns correctly structured data.
prompt: Create a Playwright API test for a GET request to {{endpoint}}. It should assert that the status code is 200 and the JSON response contains the field {{field_name}} with value {{expected_value}}.
copilot_prompt: // Playwright: API GET test for {{endpoint}} validating {{field_name}}.
explanation: API tests are faster and more reliable than UI tests for validating backend logic.
guidance: Usually used inside a file like tests/api/users.spec.ts.
before: // No API test coverage for this endpoint...

title: Mocking API Endpoints
use_case: Testing UI behavior without being dependent on a unstable or slow backend API.
prompt: Write a Playwright script that intercepts all network requests to {{api_url}} and returns a mocked JSON body {{mock_body}}. Then navigate to {{page_url}} and verify the UI shows this mocked data.
copilot_prompt: // Playwright: Mock API {{api_url}} with {{mock_body}} on page {{page_url}}.
explanation: Mocking prevents flaky tests by isolating the frontend from the backend. Ideal for testing error states.
guidance: Use this prompt within your test file before performing navigations.
before: test('real api', async ({ page }) => { ... })

title: Visual Component Snapshot
use_case: Capturing UI regressions that can't be easily caught with functional tests.
prompt: Write a Playwright test to take a visual screenshot of the component {{selector}} on the page {{url}} and compare it against the saved baseline snapshot.
copilot_prompt: // Playwright: Visual snapshot test for {{selector}} on {{url}}.
explanation: Snapshot testing ensures that any visual change (CSS, layout) is flagged for review.
guidance: Ensure you run with --update-snapshots the first time.

title: Interacting with Iframes
use_case: Testing third-party widgets like Stripe or PayPal payment inputs embedded within iframes.
prompt: Generate a Playwright test to interact with an iframe with selector {{iframe_selector}}. Inside the iframe, find the input {{input_selector}} and type {{text_to_type}}.
copilot_prompt: // Playwright: Interact with iframe {{iframe_selector}} and type in {{input_selector}}.
explanation: Standard selectors don't work across iframe boundaries. FrameLocators are required to bridge this gap.
guidance: Use frameLocator() to access elements inside iframes safely.
before: await page.fill('#card-number', '1234'); // This will fail if inside iframe!

title: Drag and Drop Automation
use_case: Testing list reordering or Kanban board interactions.
prompt: Write a Playwright script to drag the element {{source_selector}} and drop it into the container {{target_selector}}.
copilot_prompt: // Playwright: Drag {{source_selector}} to {{target_selector}}.
explanation: Playwright provides a built-in dragTo() method that handles coordinates and mouse events automatically.
guidance: Ensure source and target are visible before the action.
before: await page.mouse.down({ x: 10, y: 10 }); ...

title: Handling Multiple Browser Tabs
use_case: Verifying links that open external documentation or OAuth flows in new tabs.
prompt: Create a Playwright script that clicks a link {{link_selector}}, waits for the new tab to open, and then asserts the title of the new tab is {{expected_title}}.
copilot_prompt: // Playwright: Handle click on {{link_selector}} and check popup title {{expected_title}}.
explanation: When a new tab opens, you must capture the page object using the context.waitForEvent('page') listener.
guidance: Wait for the promise of the popup before clicking the link.
before:
await page.click('target=_blank');
// Can't access the new page easily!

title: Mobile Emulation Setup
use_case: Ensuring responsive designs work correctly on iPhone/Android device viewports.
prompt: Create a Playwright test configuration for an iPhone 13 Pro viewport. Then write a test to check if the menu toggle button is visible when navigating to {{url}}.
copilot_prompt: // Playwright: Emulate iPhone 13 Pro for {{url}} and check mobile menu.
explanation: Mobile devices have different user agents and touch capability. Playwright emulates these accurately.
guidance: Usually done via playwright.config.ts but can be done per-test using use: { ...devices['iPhone 13 Pro'] }.
before: await page.setViewportSize({ width: 375, height: 667 });

copilot_prompt: // Playwright: Upload {{file_path}} to input {{input_selector}}.

title: Network Throttling Check
use_case: Observing how the application handles slow network conditions and showing loading spinners.
prompt: Write a Playwright script using CDPSession to simulate a Slow 3G network connection. Navigate to {{url}} and verify that the loading spinner is visible for at least {{seconds}} seconds.

explanation: Simulating network conditions helps identify performance bottlenecks and UX issues in loading states.
guidance: Requires access to context.newCDPSession(page).
before: await page.goto(url); // Loads at full speed

explanation: Integrating accessibility checks into your CI/CD ensures that your app remains usable for everyone.
guidance: Install @axe-core/playwright first.

title: Accessing Shadow DOM Elements
use_case: Automating modern applications that use web components or micro-frontends.
prompt: Create a Playwright test that selects an element {{selector}} located inside an open Shadow DOM root on page {{url}}.
copilot_prompt: // Playwright: Click {{selector}} inside Shadow DOM on {{url}}.
explanation: Playwright's default selectors pierce through Shadow DOM roots automatically, unlike Selenium or basic JS.
guidance: Standard css selectors usually work directly, but use locator().first() if there are multiple roots.
before: document.querySelector('host').shadowRoot.querySelector('#el');

title: Bypassing Login via Cookies
use_case: Speeding up tests by setting valid session cookies instead of re-performing UI login every time.
prompt: Write a Playwright script that sets a cookie {{cookie_name}} with value {{cookie_value}} for domain {{domain}} before navigating to {{url}}.
copilot_prompt: // Playwright: Set auth cookie {{cookie_name}} for {{domain}} and go to {{url}}.
explanation: Directly setting authentication state via cookies or localStorage is much faster than UI login.
guidance: Use browserContext.addCookies() before navigating.
before: test('slow login', async ({ page }) => { ... await page.login() ... })

title: Global Auth Setup
use_case: Storing authentication state once to be used by hundreds of tests across the suite.
prompt: Create a Playwright global setup file called auth.setup.ts that logs into {{url}}, saves storage state to a JSON file {{state_path}}, and can be referenced in playwright.config.ts.
copilot_prompt: // Playwright: Create auth.setup.ts for {{url}} saving state to {{state_path}}.
explanation: Global Setup allows you to perform login once per run, drastically reducing overall test time.
guidance: Configure projects in playwright.config.ts to depend on this setup.
before: // Every test starts at the login page...

title: Dynamic Element Search (Regex)
use_case: Selecting elements in frameworks like Salesforce or SAP where IDs are auto-generated and change every build.
prompt: Generate a Playwright locator that finds a button with text matching the regular expression {{regex_pattern}} and clicks it.
copilot_prompt: // Playwright: Click button matching regex {{regex_pattern}}.
explanation: Regex selectors allow for robust automation when UI labels or classes change slightly (e.g., 'Welcome, User 123').
guidance: Use /regex/ syntax within getByRole or getByText.

title: Network Timeout Simulation
use_case: Verifying that the application shows a 'Took too long' message when an API is unresponsive.
prompt: Create a Playwright script that intercepts request {{api_url}} and delays the response by {{delay_ms}} milliseconds to simulate a timeout. Check for the error message on {{page_url}}.
copilot_prompt: // Playwright: Delay {{api_url}} by {{delay_ms}}ms and check for timeout on {{page_url}}.
explanation: Timeout testing ensures your app doesn't hang indefinitely and provides good feedback to users.
guidance: Use route.fulfill() with a delay or don't fulfill it at all.
before: // No way to test slow API response locally...

title: Hover and Tooltip Validation

prompt: Write a Playwright test to hover over element {{target_selector}} and assert that the tooltip with text {{tooltip_text}} becomes visible.
copilot_prompt: // Playwright: Hover {{target_selector}} and check tooltip {{tooltip_text}}.

guidance: Use .hover() and then wait for the tooltip locator.

title: CI Sharding and Parallelism
use_case: Reducing a 2-hour test suite down to 15 minutes by running across multiple machines.
prompt: Create a GitHub Actions workflow snippet that runs Playwright tests with sharding support: --shard={{current_shard}}/{{total_shards}}.
copilot_prompt: // Playwright: GitHub Action shard command for {{current_shard}} of {{total_shards}}.
explanation: Sharding is the best way to scale large test suites in CI environments.
guidance: Used in the matrix strategy of .github/workflows/main.yml.
before: run: npx playwright test
after:
strategy:
  matrix:
    shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]
run: npx playwright test --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/4
example_output:
jobs:
  test:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Run tests
        run: npx playwright test --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ strategy.job-total }}

guidance: Use page.waitForResponse() with a filter function.

title: Mocking LocalStorage State

guidance: Use addInitScript to ensure values are set before any application JS runs.
